channel.title: Bucharest Daily News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Bucharest Daily News (bucharestdailynews.com)

item.title: Buyers chase under €120K homes in 2026: Old stock surge amid price squeeze
item.description: 60% of 2026 buyers eye homes ≤€120K, 44% want old properties, 32% prefer houses over 2-room flats (30%).

item.title: Romania doubles aluminium can recycling to 75% after deposit-return system rollout
item.description: Romania’s aluminium can recycling rate jumped from 35% to 75% in 2025 after the deposit-return system launch.

item.title: Romanians demand a digital state: Online services top wish list, but pace too slow
item.description: Edge Institute survey reveals Romanians want all state interactions online, all documents in one app and medical records accessible digitally.

item.title: Romania ranks among Europe's biggest second-hand car importers
item.description: Romania ranks among Europe's biggest second-hand car importers facing VIN fraud risks, czech firm Vincario shows.

item.title: Half of Romanians skip meals amid crushing cost-of-living squeeze
item.description: 56% of Romanians cut food intake or bought cheaper groceries last year to cope financially; 60% feared running out of money for basics.

item.title: Julius Meinl secures permit for revamp of iconic Ambasador Hotel
item.description: Julius Meinl Living gets Bucharest building permit in Jan 2026 for €-multi-million redo of Art Deco Ambasador Hotel into 160-room The Julius Bucharest, opening early 2028.

item.title: British fish & chips brand Harry Ramsden’s to open first restaurant in Bucharest
item.description: Harry Ramsden’s, the legendary British fish & chips brand, debuts in Romania with a first restaurant in Bucharest’s ParkLake.

item.title: Olympus invests €7.5M in new Brașov dairy storage hall, pushing total factory spend to €217.5M
item.description: Olympus Foods starts €7.5M construction of 7,100 sqm production and storage hall at Brașov Dairy Plant. Follows €40M logistics centre; total investments hit €217.5M since 2011.

item.title: NIBIRU, Romania’s first seasonal entertainment city, opens July 16. €300M economic boost
item.description: NIBIRU launches July 16, 2026 on 1.6M sqm Romanian Black Sea coast: free promenade with 2K trees, 30+ eateries, nightly shows, NIBIRU Arena for Beach Please! festival.

item.title: 2.3 million Romanians still work abroad despite wage gains
item.description: EU Commission 2026 report: Romanians are 26% of intra-EU movers (2.3M), topping Poland/Italy. Italy/Spain/Germany top destinations.
